focus: Raising accuracy and lowering cost: model-arm cost shape, census read waste, aggregation sweep, payload flaw, adaptive reruns
noveltyJustification: Aggregation sweep, 8667-to-82 doc-reader ratio, adaptive-rerun arithmetic and the bare-evidence payload flaw are new; cost and counterfactual scoring extend iteration 1
keyQuestions: Q2: How can the scan's accuracy be raised or its cost lowered?

title: Model arm is cheap: 121 calls, 40.9s total wall, p50 326ms; ~40.7k planned input tokens across 3 reruns; the git-heavy census (~171s) and draw (~381s) dominate
The census spawns one git show per tracked skill doc: 8667 docs read to find citations in 82 (0.95%); the draw re-reads the same tree
Zero-call accuracy win: min(reruns)<0.5 gives TP 27 FP 0; mean<0.6 gives TP 29 FP 1 FN 2 (acc 0.925, recall 0.935), all inside the keep rule's precision allowance
One miss is a payload flaw: the judgment unit is a single line; live-17's sentence is a bare Evidence pointer, 3 of 20 live rows carry no claim at all
The only new FP under mean<0.6 is live-18 (0.50/0.50/0.52), a genuine borderline row whose window does contain the claim's subject; the strict < 0.5 is load-bearing
Adaptive reruns: 12 of 40 rows touch [0.35,0.65], 26 are fully confident; screen-then-confirm would use ~65 calls vs 121 while preserving the flip signal
The instruction hash and keep rule are pre-registered gates while requalification watches only provider/model; any prompt or row-set change silently changes what was measured

direction: Fewer reruns will fix the misses
reason: First-rerun-only scoring is worse (acc 0.850 vs 0.875); the reruns earn their keep, the aggregation is what is leaving catches on the table

direction: The misses are pure model error
reason: live-17 is a payload flaw: the model receives a bare Evidence pointer line with no claim, and still one of the five misses remains genuinely ambiguous
